claim: Ontology injection beats RAG at matched context budget

evidence.quote: C3 injects ∼2,800–3,200 tokens versus C2's ∼2,000, a 40–60% overhead on structural scaffolding
The C2–C3 post-hoc comparison was not significant on any metric (pcorr > 0.20)
on the primary model's grand means C2 scores at or above C3 on TF, MA, and RC; only RS shows a consistent ontology advantage
we increased the number of retrieved text chunks for RAG to match the total number of input tokens retrieved by Community-GraphRAG

note: No study runs ontology injection against RAG at a matched budget. The available evidence contradicts the claim: in 2604.00555 the ontology arm had 40-60% more tokens and still scored at or below RAG (grand means .77 vs .83), not significant. In the one total-token-matched graph study (2502.11371, GraphRAG not ontology), the overall graph advantage vanished. Refuted as stated; a true matched ontology run is still absent.

claim: Non-entailment of the negation is a sufficient validity criterion

evidence.quote: O is consistent (or satisfiable) w.r.t. D if a model of O w.r.t. D and V exists.
it may simply be missing (but possibly true), following the open-world assumption.
That is, an output is valid if and only if the ontology does not entail its negation
Supported and Not-supported respectively indicate Wikipedia supports the fact and does not support the fact (either contradicts or does not contain any evidence).

note: O ⊭ ¬a is consistency of O plus a; under the open-world assumption it passes every claim the ontology neither entails nor refutes, including fabricated type-compatible facts. Every support metric checked (AIS, FActScore, RAGAS, ALCE, SummaC, AlignScore) fails that case; FEVER keeps it as NotEnoughInfo.

claim: Structure, not context volume, explains the reported gains

evidence.quote: A controlled budget-equalized experiment isolating the format effect from the volume effect remains future work
accuracy decreases with length for all models
No triples-vs-prose study with explicit token-length matching was found.

note: Not supported. No budget-equalized, ontology-as-prose, or permuted-structure control exists. Extra length tends to hurt, so volume alone would not explain a gain, but added facts could. In 2604.00555 there was no ontology-over-RAG gain to explain.

claim: Format effects (triples versus verbalized text) are smaller than the effect of including the knowledge at all

evidence.quote: no knowledge 60.58, raw triples 93.19, Flan-T5 KG-to-text 97.71
LLMs prefer receiving textual knowledge
performance differences of up to 76 accuracy points

note: Confirmed for KGQA in one study (inclusion about 30-75 points, format about 1-8). The first quote is the research note's transcription of table values, not author prose. Formatting-only noise can still be large on fragile models (2310.11324), so single-template comparisons are unreliable.

claim: Standard faithfulness and attribution metrics treat neither-entailed-nor-contradicted claims as unsupported

evidence.quote: Annotators are instructed to only mark output as attributable if it is clear that all parts can be directly inferred from the source.
Supported and Not-supported respectively indicate Wikipedia supports the fact and does not support the fact (either contradicts or does not contain any evidence).
the claims that are made in the answer can be inferred from the context
the probability of the model predicting the aligned label in the 3-way classification setting

note: FEVER (1803.05355) is the exception: it keeps NotEnoughInfo as a separate label, recalled from the abstract, not re-fetched.

claim: Padding prompt length with no new needed information degrades accuracy

evidence.quote: from 0.92 to 0.68
degrades substantially (13.9%--85%) as input length increases

note: 2402.14848 pads 250 to 3,000 tokens; the 2,000 to 3,000 step alone was not isolated. Counterpoint: random unrelated documents raised RAG accuracy by up to 35% (2401.14887), so the filler type matters.
